```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Build the cohort design

`nis_design()` validates `YEAR`, `HOSP_NIS`, `NIS_STRATUM`, and `DISCWT`,
then constructs a survey design before applying the declared domain.
Existing dplyr groups (including rowwise grouping) are removed first, for both
data frames and lazy DuckDB queries. Aggregate cohort expressions such as
`LOS > mean(LOS)` use the full input rather than each input group. To use a
group-specific threshold, compute an explicit cohort indicator upstream and
pass that column to `cohort`. Group the returned survey design when you need
grouped survey summaries.

```{r design}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure & AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, LOS),
  annualize = TRUE
)
srvyr::summarise(design, total = srvyr::survey_total(),
                 mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS))
```

The output contains a weighted fixture total and mean LOS with design-based
standard errors. Hospital placeholders account for hospital-years with no
cohort discharges in the variance calculation. The returned design exposes
only cohort discharges to summaries. This placeholder strategy is experimental.

For lazy inputs, DuckDB computes hospital-year strata, invalid-field counts,
and annualization coverage in one sample scan. The separate cohort scan
collects the selected columns needed to build the survey design in R.

## Analyze a domain within the cohort

The object returned by `nis_design()` is already an srvyr survey design. Use
`dplyr::filter()` on that object to define an analytic domain. Like
`subset()` on a survey design, it uses the original sampling structure for
variance. Hospitals with no domain discharges contribute zero, including
when an entire stratum falls outside the domain.

On the design returned by `nis_design()`, `filter()` also removes
out-of-domain records from the stored analysis data. The survey design
retains the original sampled hospital counts for variance estimation, so
there is no separate compaction step. If you no longer need the wider
design, assign the filtered result back to the same variable.

```{r domain}
design |>
  dplyr::filter(AGE >= 65) |>
  dplyr::group_by(YEAR) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS),
    discharges = srvyr::unweighted(dplyr::n())
  )
```

`discharges` counts only observed domain discharges. The filtered design
can also be passed directly to survey functions and to
`gtsummary::tbl_svysummary()`.

Filtering the lazy input before `nis_design()` restricts the records
available to construct the design and can remove entire hospitals or strata.
To define a cohort within the available sample, pass the inclusion criteria
to `cohort`. To narrow an existing design to a subpopulation, filter the
returned design.

## Choose a pooling convention

Without annualization, pooled-year weights represent the combined included
period. `annualize = TRUE` divides by the number of valid years; partial years
count as a year. When quarter fields are present the function warns about
incomplete year coverage and a 2015 cohort restricted to one coding era.
Exclude partial years or choose a documented alternative if this convention
does not fit the estimand.

## Run a weighted sensitivity analysis

Use the original survey design for national totals. The example below
compares the original mean LOS difference with one weighted to balance the
observed age distribution between groups. It uses invented data and targets
the age distribution of the pooled adult discharge population. The
propensity model uses age as its only predictor.

```{r reweight}
original <- nis_design(nis, AGE >= 18, keep = c(AGE, LOS, heart_failure))
propensity <- survey::svyglm(
  heart_failure ~ AGE, design = original, family = quasibinomial()
)
p <- stats::predict(propensity, newdata = original$variables, type = "response")
stopifnot(all(is.finite(p) & p > 0 & p < 1))

weighted <- nis_reweight(original, ifelse(heart_failure, 1 / p, 1 / (1 - p)))
age_by_group <- function(design) {
  survey::svyby(~AGE, ~heart_failure, design, survey::svymean)
}
los_contrast <- function(design) {
  fit <- survey::svyglm(LOS ~ heart_failure, design)
  summary(fit)$coefficients["heart_failureTRUE", c("Estimate", "Std. Error")]
}

age_by_group(original)
age_by_group(weighted)
rbind(original = los_contrast(original), reweighted = los_contrast(weighted))
srvyr::summarise(original, national_discharges = srvyr::survey_total())
```

`nis_reweight()` is experimental. It multiplies the survey weights by the
supplied factors, in the order of the design rows. The weighted mean
contrast and its standard error use that transformed design. This variance
treats the supplied factors as fixed. Report the propensity specification,
weight range, any trimming or exclusions, and balance in the variables used
to justify the sensitivity analysis. The age means illustrate one balance
check. The example uses all weights without trimming. Causal interpretation
would require a justified exposure definition, target population, and
assumptions about confounding and overlap.

## Why design-based standard errors matter

NIS uses hospital clusters, strata, and discharge weights. Ordinary means and
standard errors treat rows as if they came from a simple random sample and
do not reflect that structure. Use `srvyr` or `survey` methods on the returned
design for point estimates and uncertainty. A survey standard error is an
estimate of sampling variability under the supplied design, not a guarantee
that all sources of bias have been addressed.

## Inspect exclusions

Rows with missing, non-finite, or non-positive design fields are excluded
before the cohort is applied. Inspect the aggregate audit attribute and report
the exclusions with the analysis.

```{r exclusions}
attr(design, "nis_excluded")
```

This list gives counts by field and year, not record-level information.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - Treating annualized weights as a correction for arbitrary partial-year
>   coverage.
> - Using non-survey summaries for estimates or uncertainty.
> - Treating reweighting or placeholder-row variance methods as established
>   methods; both are experimental.

See [`nis_design()`](../reference/nis_design.html),
[`nis_reweight()`](../reference/nis_reweight.html), and [Data notes by year](year-notes.html).
